title: Guards judge what actually runs
text: Bash guards split a command with the shared quote-aware splitter and judge only the word in command position. A quoted search pattern such as `rg 'a|pytest|b'` and a heredoc body fed to a typed `yoke` command are data, so neither is a writer or a `python -c` invocation. `git stash list` and `git stash show` are reads; other stash actions still change state. `yoke watch <kind> --print-streaming-pair` before `--` only prints its pair, so it needs no watcher timeout. The argv a direct `yoke qa mission host-command ... --` call ships runs on the Test Machine, so the path-claim guard does not fail closed on an `sh -c` there; a redirect or substitution still runs locally and stays enforced. Observed in source and tests; deployed harness proof is pending.
